title: Console metrics materialized views for SLO & cost attribution
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: The Console team needs curated, high-performance artifacts in the data warehouse that directly support SLO attribution, per-route/per-customer latency and error breakdowns, and token-level cost estimation. Current ad-hoc queries against raw event streams (console_events, api_token_usage, route_latency_samples) are slow, duplicate-sensitive, and expensive at scale. This ticket defines a set of materialized views and transformation patterns to replace heavyweight queries and serve dashboards and downstream ML jobs.

Goals: Create a small set of well-partitioned, tested materialized views (daily and hourly) that provide: (1) per-customer/per-route SLO metrics (p50/p95/p99, error rates), (2) per-model and per-route token cost breakdowns, (3) attribution for Dedicated vs Hosted traffic, and (4) stable foreign-key-ready dimensions for join efficiency. Views should be queryable with sub-second response for common dashboard filters and refresh within our freshness SLO (hourly for hourly views, daily for daily aggregates).

Data sources: console_events (ingested via Kafka->raw table), api_token_usage (billing/usage events), route_latency_samples (sampled latencies), model_variant_mapping (catalog), dedicated_capacity_allocations.

Design summary:
- New materialized views: mv_console_slo_attribution_hourly, mv_console_cost_breakdown_hourly, mv_console_slo_attribution_daily, mv_console_route_latency_histograms_daily.
- Partitioning: hourly views partitioned by ingestion_hour (timestamp truncated to hour), daily views by event_date.
- Clustering: cluster by customer_id, route_id to accelerate common filters.
- Keys: use deterministic event_id and canonicalize token counts so views are idempotent on re-ingest.
- Freshness strategy: incremental dbt models (incremental merge) for hourly; full-refresh for daily during low-traffic window on Sunday 03:00 UTC for re-compute and compaction.
- Retention & compaction: maintain 13 months for daily views and 90 days for hourly; older data moved to console_dw_archive.
- Cost calculation: join token-per-output metrics from api_token_usage with route attribution heuristics; expose estimated USD token cost and GPU-time proxy (ms * gpu_factor).

Operational requirements: create freshness monitors (Prometheus alert via metadata job), add a runbook for manual repair (rebuild partitions, re-run merges), set RBAC so only analytics and observability services can refresh materialized views. Include unit tests: row counts sanity, p95 monotonicity tests, null-rate checks.

Dependencies: needs model_variant_mapping stable IDs (ENG-5980), and data quality fixes in console_events dedup (ENG-6052).
acceptance_criteria: mv_console_slo_attribution_hourly exists and is populated for last 72 hours
Common console dashboards (SLO heatmap, latency by route, cost leaderboards) query the new views and show <= 2s load for typical filters
Hourly refresh job completes within 10 minutes and reports freshness metric to observability
DBT models have tests (unique keys, not_null on customer_id, p95 sanity check) and pass in CI
Cost estimates validate against billing dataset within 5% for a sample customer over a 7-day window
Runbook and alerting for stale or failed refresh exist in Confluence and PagerDuty playbook linked
notes: Trade-offs: near-real-time streaming materialized views would increase compute costs substantially; hourly incremental strikes a balance for 90% of dashboards.
Dedup: rely on deterministic event_id + ingestion_source to dedupe; any remaining duplicates flagged for downstream cleanup job.
Kernel selection: prefer BigQuery partitioned tables (or Snowflake materialized views depending on final infra decision); keep schema portable and dbt-first.
Follow-ups: consider a compacted 15-min rollup for high-load customers in a later ticket if latency requirements tighten.
Owner: Analytics eng (Rafael) for implementation; Console product (Maya Patel) to validate dashboards; Observability (Kendall) for alerting
